one_liner: An 86-year-old female with respiratory failure, malnutrition, and drainage from an old PEG site underwent successful insertion of a right femoral triple lumen catheter for total parenteral nutrition access without complications.

problems.name: Drainage of an old percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy site

procedures.name: Insertion of a right femoral triple lumen catheter
procedures.outcome: The patient tolerated the full procedure well. There were no complications.

course.narrative: An 86-year-old ventilator-dependent female requiring total parenteral nutrition due to dysphagia and malnutrition needed central venous access. Consent was obtained from the patient's legal guardian. Under local anesthesia with 1% lidocaine, a right femoral triple lumen catheter was successfully placed using the Seldinger technique with guidewire insertion. Correct placement was confirmed via dark venous blood aspiration and back-bleeding from all ports, which were then flushed, locked, and sutured in place with sterile dressing applied. The procedure was uncomplicated, well tolerated, and the nurse was notified for access.

action_items.action: Allow for access of the triple lumen catheter
action_items.rationale: Catheter insertion completed for total parenteral nutrition.
